source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** A rule is valid when the trimmed recognized text has 1–100 characters, contains no line break, tab or `;`, and does not start with `#`; and the trimmed replacement has 1–500 characters and contains no line break or tab. conclusions.rationale: The exchange decision explicitly gives tab priority, first-semicolon split, semicolon-only first-significant-line headers, trimmed comments, literal replacement semicolons and LF export. Canonical bulk header prevents losing a genuine header-shaped first rule; BOM/CRLF and scalar-limit tests are planned.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** The exchange format is UTF-8 text with one rule per line. A line containing a tab splits on its first tab; otherwise it splits on its first `;`. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. The first line that is neither blank nor a comment is ignored as a header when it equals (case-insensitively, after trimming) `texte_reconnu;remplacement` or `recognized;replacement`. Export writes the header `recognized;replacement`, then one `recognized;replacement` line per rule in list order; because AC-002 forbids tab, `;` and a leading `#` in recognized text and tab in replacements, every valid rule set round-trips. Replacement text may contain `;`. CSV quoting is not supported; spreadsheet copy and paste uses the tab separator.

plan_citations.excerpt: If a line contains a tab, split at its first tab even if a semicolon precedes it; otherwise split at the first semicolon.

conclusions.rationale: Merge retains existing recognized spelling/id/position and updates only replacement; replace adopts input order and reconciles ids by key. The bounded reader rejects invalid UTF-8/oversized input before pure parsing, and transactions use atomic durable replacement with explicit no-write faults. Oversized valid-set exports remain format-lossless but correctly refused by the separate specified file cap.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Import accepts a file up to 1 MB in merge or replace mode. Merge updates the replacement of rules whose normalized key matches, keeps their position, and appends new rules in file order. Replace makes the file content the whole rule set in file order. Duplicate keys inside one file or block are errors. Import is atomic: on any error, unreadable file or persistence failure, saved rules are unchanged. Export then replace-import of the same file reproduces the same rules and order.

plan_citations.excerpt: Merge keeps matched existing recognized spelling, ID and position, updates only replacement, and appends new rules in file order.

conclusions.rationale: Full C+F folding with original UTF-8 offsets avoids substring matches inside expansions, collapses Unicode whitespace runs and evaluates Unicode-category boundaries on original neighbors. Pinned script categories include one-sided Han/kana/hangul exemptions and supplementary/halfwidth/decomposed fixtures; literal bytes/separators are preserved.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Matching is case-insensitive (Unicode case folding) and the replacement is inserted exactly as written. A match must start and end on word boundaries: the characters immediately before and after the match are not Unicode letters or digits, or are the text edges. On a side where the recognized text begins or ends with a CJK ideograph, kana or hangul character, no boundary check applies, because those scripts are written without spaces. A whitespace run inside the recognized text matches any non-empty whitespace run; other characters match literally. Punctuation adjacent to a match is kept.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Rules apply in one left-to-right pass over the final recognized text. At each position the rule with the longest normalized key wins; ties follow list order. Rules apply after speech recognition, language detection and Chinese script conversion, and before the existing approximate custom-word correction, filler removal, normalization and AI post-processing. Approximate correction never alters a span produced by a replacement. The inserted text and the history text include the replacements. Rules committed from the UI or the CLI apply from the next dictation of the running app. An empty rule set leaves text unchanged.
